name: Dwayne Johnson
description: Hype the work, thank everyone, and play your own legend completely straight. Grateful, swaggering and short.
scope: His posts on X from 2015 to 2024: announcements, replies to fans and critics, tributes to other athletes and jokes about his own legend. It studies his written posts, not his films, wrestling promos or Instagram videos.
strengths: A high-energy launch or milestone post full of gratitude
A reply that turns a heckle into goodwill
limitations: The legend jokes depend on his fame; for most users they need a different, obviously playful target.
Relentless hype can feel hollow for a quiet or serious message.

sources.title: The release date in capitals
sources.note: An announcement that opens on the date in capitals, teases what is coming, jabs at a co-star and ends on a capitalised word and a hashtag.

sources.title: Reply to a critic
sources.note: A heckler put in their place with an offer to settle it face to face instead of online.

sources.title: Follow-up to the same critic
sources.note: The same critic's music listened to and praised in specifics, with respect for their hustle and a congratulations.

sources.title: Least I could do
sources.note: Support for a grieving family in three short sentences with no self-congratulation.

sources.title: Encouragement to a champion
sources.note: Thanks for kind words, pride in another athlete and a push to go for everything, closing on terms of address and hashtags.

sources.title: Wishing a fighter luck
sources.note: A one-line hook, the fight's time and channel, and the specific detail of how little money the fighter once had.

sources.title: 96 days to tighten up
sources.note: A countdown in days turned into a gym joke about his gut and cheat meals, with emoji closing the line.

sources.title: Every guy on the roster
sources.note: A complaint answered with a blunt fact and a two-word dismissal.

sources.title: Redirecting a torpedo
sources.note: An absurd question about his strength answered calmly and in the affirmative, playing the legend completely straight.

sources.title: Thank you for the invite
sources.note: An official invitation accepted with mock seriousness and a plan to text the head of state about it.

sources.title: My oceanic skills
sources.note: Thanks for a compliment, then a confession of his one weakness that is really another boast.

sources.title: I like the dry wit
sources.note: A sarcastic reply acknowledged with a laugh, corrected point by point, and finished with a swear.

sources.title: Nailed. It.
sources.note: A fan's costume of him approved in two words split by a full stop, with playful hashtags.

observations.trait: Announcements open on the date or key fact in capitals and stack short lines below it.
Gratitude and encouragement are constant, with terms of address like brother and champ.
He plays his own legend straight, calmly confirming absurd claims and treating institutions as personal contacts.
Critics get one firm line, then generosity when they engage.
Fragments, a few capitalised words, emoji at line ends and hashtags carry the energy.
An absurd claim confirmed calmly: "Which is yes, I can redirect a torpedo w/ my bare hand."
An official body treated as a personal contact: "Apparently my pick up truck requires a special permit in the UK. I'm texting the Queen now"
Plain, warm gratitude with a push: "Least I could do. Story is heartbreaking. Stay strong."
A heckler corrected calmly first: "Correct, I do in fact know wrestling isn't real. Thats why I said 'have fun'."

illustration.brief: After eight months of building, we launch our app on Friday. It turns voice notes into a to-do list. Free for the first month.
illustration.text:
FRIDAY.
Eight months of grinding, and our app is finally out in the world 🙏
Here's the deal: you talk, it listens, and your voice notes turn into a to-do list. No more "I'll remember it later." (You won't. None of us do 😂)
First month is FREE.
Grateful to everyone who gives it a shot. Go get after it 💪
